No copy stays in guard-edits.py: it keeps _CASE_BLIND, _config_verdict and the verdict words, and calls _config.audit_config_way at its two sites (edit tools, MCP). No existing _config name changed behaviour; only os calls are used, nothing imported. journal-writes._classify_placed now reads `if _config.audit_config_way(tree):` instead of `rel == _config.CONFIG_REL`; the row keeps its event name, keys and shape, target the path as placed, no key added. (2) RULE 2: for a creating write that is config-shaped once case is set aside, _case_walk walks from the tree's root one component at a time: an exact component is followed; a case-only difference is judged in the directory that holds it - by _one_entry (lstat identity) where the config's own name exists there, else by that directory's rule (_volume_folds, memoised per call), a directory the write would create taking the rule of the one it would be created in; an unanswerable question gives case-blind (held, stated words). The walk starts only after the existing string shape test and the existing early returns, so the ordinary path is untouched. (3) RULE 3: tests/test_guard_edits.py's counter (_disk_calls) wraps one table (_DISK_CALLS: os.stat/lstat/readlink/listdir/scandir/access and os.path exists/lexists/isdir/isfile/islink/ismount/realpath/samefile/getsize/getmtime), counting leaf calls; cf29 now asserts kind-for-kind equality with the sequence before the walk, zero listings, total no more than before identity, for an existing source file, a new one and a plain-folder config-named file; cf30 reads guard-edits.py and the _config functions audit_config_way reaches (AST, transitive) and names any os./os.path. call in neither _DISK_CALLS nor _NOT_DISK.
